questions.title: GATE IT 2004 | Question: 72
questions.subject: Unknown
questions.questionHtml:
What is the availability of a software with the following reliability figures?
Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) = 25 days
Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) = 6 hours

  1. 1%
  2. 24%
  3. 99%
  4. $99.009\%$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: Converted 25 days to 600 hours; availability is 600/(600+6)=100/101=99.00990099...%. Stored key and GateOverflow answer are D; the listed value 99.009% is truncated, not conventionally rounded.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE CSE 2004 | Question: 73
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The inclusion of which of the following sets into

$S = \left\{ \left\{1, 2\right\}, \left\{1, 2, 3\right\}, \left\{1, 3, 5\right\}, \left\{1, 2, 4\right\}, \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\right\} \right\} $

is necessary and sufficient to make $S$ a complete lattice under the partial order defined by set containment?

  1. $\{1\}$
  2. $\{1\}, \{2, 3\}$
  3. $\{1\}, \{1, 3\}$
  4. $\{1\}, \{1, 3\}, \{1, 2, 3, 4\}, \{1, 2, 3, 5\}$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: Adding {1} supplies the missing meet for incomparable pairs; all joins already exist. The resulting finite lattice is complete. Stored key and GateOverflow answer are A.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE CSE 2004 | Question: 74
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
An examination paper has $150$ multiple choice questions of one mark each, with each question having four choices. Each incorrect answer fetches $-0.25$ marks. Suppose $1000$ students choose all their answers randomly with uniform probability. The sum total of the expected marks obtained by all these students is

  1. $0$
  2. $2550$
  3. $7525$
  4. $9375$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: Per question expectation is 1/4-(3/4)(1/4)=1/16; total is 150*1000/16=9375. Stored key and GateOverflow answer are D.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE CSE 2004 | Question: 75
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Mala has the colouring book in which each English letter is drawn two times. She wants to paint each of these $52$ prints with one of $k$ colours, such that the colour pairs used to colour any two letters are different. Both prints of a letter can also be coloured with the same colour. What is the minimum value of $k$ that satisfies this requirement?

  1. $9$
  2. $8$
  3. $7$
  4. $6$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: Under the conventional unordered-pair interpretation, k colors give k(k+1)/2 pairs; k=6 gives 21<26 and k=7 gives 28. GateOverflow discusses the wording ambiguity; the answer-key interpretation is unordered and gives C.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE CSE 2004 | Question: 76
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
In an $M \times N$ matrix all non-zero entries are covered in $a$ rows and $b$ columns. Then the maximum number of non-zero entries, such that no two are on the same row or column, is

  1. $\leq a +b$
  2. $\leq \max(a, b)$
  3. $\leq \min(M-a, N-b)$
  4. $\leq \min(a, b)$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: A set of nonzero positions with no repeated row or column has size at most a and at most b, hence at most min(a,b). Stored key and GateOverflow answer are D.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE CSE 2004 | Question: 77
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The minimum number of colours required to colour the following graph, such that no two adjacent vertices are assigned the same color, is

  1. $2$
  2. $3$
  3. $4$
  4. $5$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: Inspected the local graph image. Triangles imply at least three colors; checking whether outer top and bottom vertices share a color shows a 3-coloring impossible. A valid 4-coloring exists. Stored key and GateOverflow answer are C.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE CSE 2004 | Question: 78
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Two $n$ bit binary strings, $S_1$ and $S_2$ are chosen randomly with uniform probability. The probability that the Hamming distance between these strings (the number of bit positions where the two strings differ) is equal to $d$ is

  1. $\dfrac{^{n}C_{d}}{2^{n}}$

  2. $\dfrac{^{n}C_{d}}{2^{d}}$

  3. $\dfrac{d}{2^{n}}$

  4. $\dfrac{1}{2^{d}}$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: For fixed S1, choose d of n positions to flip in S2; each S2 is uniform among 2^n strings, so probability is C(n,d)/2^n. Stored key and GateOverflow answer are A.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE CSE 2004 | Question: 80
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
A point is randomly selected with uniform probability in the $X-Y$ plane within the rectangle with corners at $(0,0), (1,0), (1,2)$ and $(0,2).$ If $p$ is the length of the position vector of the point, the expected value of $p^{2}$ is

  1. $\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)$
  2. $\quad 1$
  3. $\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)$
  4. $\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: On [0,1]x[0,2], E[X^2]=1/3 and E[Y^2]=4/3; linearity gives E[p^2]=5/3. Stored key and GateOverflow answer are D.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE IT 2004 | Question: 89
questions.subject: Other / Optional
questions.questionHtml:
Consider an XML file called intro.xml and a document type definition (DTD) file intro.dtd as follows:

A validating parser will classify intro.xml as

  1. Well-formed and validated
  2. Well-formed but not validated
  3. Validated but not well-formed
  4. Neither validated nor well-formed

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: GateOverflow and a separate secondary transcription both display the DTD declaration with whitespace inside <!ELEMENT>. W3C XML 1.0 requires the contiguous markup token. The accessible copies are not the original GATE scan, so the stored key and posted answer A are not enough to resolve the stem/key conflict. Keep on HOLD until the original paper image is verified or the stem is corrected.
review.finalDisposition: HOLD: available transcriptions reproduce malformed DTD; original paper scan or verified correction required

questions.title: GATE IT 2004 | Question: 90
questions.subject: Other / Optional
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are several usages of the anchor tag in HTML.

  1. <A HREF = "http://www.gate.ac.in/HTML/BASIC/testpage.html">Test Me</A>
  2. <A HREF = "/BASIC/testpage.html">Test Me</A>
  3. <A HREF = "testpage.html">Test Me</A>
  4. <A HREF = "testpage.html#test">Test Me</A>

Which of the above are valid?

  1. I and II only
  2. I and III only
  3. I, II and III only
  4. I, II, III and IV

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: An absolute URI, root-relative path, document-relative path, and document-relative reference with a fragment are valid URI-reference forms. RFC 3986 supports relative references and fragments. Stored key and GateOverflow answer are D.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE CSE 2003 | Question: 3
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $P(E)$ denote the probability of the event $E$. Given $P(A) = 1$, $P(B) =\dfrac{1}{2}$, the values of $P(A\mid B)$ and $P(B\mid A)$ respectively are

  1. $\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right),\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$
  2. $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right),\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$
  3. $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right),{1}$
  4.   ${1},\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: Since P(A)=1, P(A complement)=0 and P(A intersection B)=P(B)=1/2. Thus P(A|B)=1 and P(B|A)=1/2. Stored key and GateOverflow answer are D.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard

questions.title: GATE CSE 2003 | Question: 4
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $A$ be a sequence of $8$ distinct integers sorted in ascending order. How many distinct pairs of sequences, $B$ and $C$ are there such that

  1. each is sorted in ascending order,
  2. $B$ has $5$ and $C$ has $3$ elements, and
  3. the result of merging $B$ and $C$ gives $A$
  1. $2$
  2. $30$
  3. $56$
  4. $256$

review.answerKeySource: data/answers/answers_by_question_uid_v1.json; independently compared with the GateOverflow page answer
review.verificationNotes: Choose which 5 of the 8 distinct elements go to B; both B and its complement C then have a unique ascending order. C(8,5)=56. Stored key and GateOverflow answer are C.
review.integrationResult: INTEGRATED in AUTHENTIC_PATCHES, practicepaper registry, and public detail shard
